title: On-call escalation timeline for pin failures and regional fallback
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is an operations-first runbook draft that maps timelines and operator actions for region pin / residency enforcement failures. Focus is on: 1) detection windows, 2) on-call response choreography across SRE, routing, and legal/contract teams, 3) customer-facing status cadence and minimal safe fallbacks.

Audience:
Primary: SREs and on-call engineers handling region-pin enforcement and routing fallbacks. Secondary: Solutions Eng, Customer Success, Legal SOC for contractual escalation.

Context and summary:
- Problem: tenant/tenant-group pin not applied or enforcement layer failing (examples: pin lookup mismatch, anchor-zone unavailable, soft-pin cache corruption, KMS region mismatch).
- Goal: detect within 2 minutes, route to fallback region within 5 minutes for non-sensitive tenants, and escalate to cross-functional on-call for anything that requires human review or legal exceptions.
- Tradeoff principle: prefer quick, auditable fallback over indefinite failure. If a tenant is contractually pinned to region A and enforcement fails, we must attempt local recovery first, then fall back to the next-compliant tier (e.g., regional mirror in same jurisdiction) or quarantine and notify customer depending on sensitivity.

Severity levels and decision matrix:
- Sev 1 (data-leak risk / cross-border violation): enforcement mismatch where requests would cross into a disallowed jurisdiction. Action: immediate page to SRE + Routing lead + Legal. 0-2 minute detection, execute quarantine flow (block routing) and collect evidence.
- Sev 2 (service degradation affecting pinned tenants): pinned requests failing or elevated error rate but routing remains local. Action: page SRE and Routing in parallel, rollback recent config, attempt cache purge and pin reapply. Target MTTR: 15–30 minutes.
- Sev 3 (partial telemetry gaps, non-user-facing anomalies): investigate during regular shift, create ticket, schedule follow-up.

Detection signals (what to alert on):
- Enforcement discrepancy metric: % of requests where tenant.region_assertion != routing.effective_region > 0.1% over 1m.
- Pin-apply failure errors from pin-service (HTTP 5xx, DB timeouts).
- Anchor-zone heartbeat missing for > 60s.
- KMS region mismatch or key-not-found errors when decrypting tenant metadata.
- Telemetry showing sudden drop in cache-hit-for-prefetch for pinned tenants.
- Customer support tickets flagged with "region mismatch" tag.

Immediate operator checklist (first 10 minutes):
1) Acknowledge pager, note timestamp.
2) Run quick health checks: ping anchor-zone, check pin-service logs (last 5m), query pin mapping for affected tenant(s). Commands: "/bin/pin-check --tenant $TENANT --last 10m" and "/bin/anchor-heartbeat --zone $ZONE".
3) If pin-service DB is unavailable: trigger DB failover per DB runbook and escalate DB-oncall.
4) If anchor-zone unreachable but KMS is OK: mark region as degraded and attempt routing to local mirror in same legal boundary (pre-approved fallback mapping). Execute: route-policy set --tenant $TENANT --fallback mirror-region.
5) If action would route outside contractual territory: DO NOT reroute. Instead, quarantine (deny new requests, drain existing) and immediately notify Legal & CS.
6) Collect evidence bundle: request IDs, timestamps, raw logs, and telemetry snapshot. Upload to secure evidence bucket and add link to incident.

Fallback orchestration patterns:
- Soft-fallback (automatic): for tenants flagged as "soft-pin-eligible" (low compliance requirement), system automatically chooses the nearest same-jurisdiction replica after TTL. Telemetry must be captured for every fallback decision.
- Hard-pinning (manual): tenants with contractual hard-pins require on-call human sign-off before any cross-region fallback. Sign-off flow involves Legal approval recorded in incident notes.

Customer communication template (first 30 minutes):
Subject: Temporary service impact for region pin enforcement for <tenant_name>
Hi <Customer Contact>,
We detected an enforcement issue that may affect where your requests are being served. Our on-call team is investigating and has activated recovery flows. We will provide an update within 30 minutes. If you have contractual restrictions preventing any fallback, please confirm immediately.
(Include link to incident evidence bundle and assigned incident number)

Escalation timeline (recommended):
- 0–2 minutes: Detection and automatic triage. Pager to SRE.
- 2–10 minutes: Operator runs immediate checklist. If unresolved => page Routing lead.
- 10–30 minutes: If routing workaround applied or DB failover in progress, notify CS and Legal. If cannot remediate automatically, trigger conference bridge with SRE + Routing + Solutions Eng.
- 30–60 minutes: If still unresolved and tenant service degraded or violating contract, escalate to Director-level on-call and prepare customer-facing Status Update.
- >60 minutes: Consider temporary regional isolation (quarantine) and initiate customer-level contract remediation process.

Runbook snippets and quick play commands (copypasta for on-call):
- pin-check: returns mapping and last-write time. Usage: pin-check --tenant $T --verbose
- pin-reapply: attempt to rebind tenant to anchor region. Usage: pin-reapply --tenant $T --force --source logs/last-write
- route-policy set: set run-time routing override for tenant. Usage: route-policy set --tenant $T --mode fallback --region <region>
- evidence-push: package and push to secure bucket. Usage: evidence-push --incident $INC --files /var/logs/pin* --meta "oncall Aisha"

Telemetry and required traces to attach:
- request trace for 10 affected requests spanning 2-minute window
- pin-service write and read latency histograms for last 30m
- routing decision table snapshot and active policy rules
- KMS key usage logs and key region metadata
- operator step log (annotate actions taken and timestamps)

Cross-functional coordination checklist:
- SRE: root cause investigation, rollback or apply mitigation.
- Routing: evaluate and apply safe fallback or route-policy override.
- DB: if pin DB is the issue, run failover and validate entries; capture integrity checksums.
- Legal: assess contract implications and approve or deny cross-border fallback.
- CS: prepare customer comms and collect consent if required.

Post-incident handoff and deliverables (within 72 hours):
- RCA draft in Confluence with timeline and evidence bundle link.
- Implement telemetry improvements for earlier detection if blindspot found.
- Create follow-up tickets: pin-service hardening, anchor-zone redundancy, KMS region validation hooks.
- Update tenant metadata: add explicit fallback tiers for each pinned tenant where permitted.

Open questions / decisions to capture:
- Define exact threshold for automatic quarantine vs. automatic fallback for medium-sensitivity tenants. (Owner: Lina)
- Add a signed-off list of pre-approved fallback regions for contractual hard-pins vs soft-pins. (Owner: Solutions Eng)
- Explore options for encrypted evidence snapshots that avoid exporting any customer PII when handing packets to Legal. (Owner: Security)

Notes to self / operator tips (informal):
- When in doubt, take screenshots of the routing table and pin mapping UI before applying overrides. They disappear after policy refresh.
- Keep customer-facing messages high-level; Legal will add contract language if needed.
- There are flakey false-positives from the anchoring telemetry during maintenance windows — check maintenance calendar before paging Director.

References and useful links:
- pin-service README (internal)
- routing policy docs (confluence link in linked_artifacts)
- JIRA-PIN-1021: simulation harness for anchor failover

Next steps (this doc):
- Move to in_review after one on-call rotation dry-run.
- Add tabletop scenario notes and annotated timeline (owner: Diego).

Revision history:
- 2025-02-10 Aisha: initial draft
- 2025-03-18 Lina: added decision thresholds and commands
